outcomes.title: Comprehend and respond personally and critically to texts
outcomes.description: - Comprehend and respond personally and critically to texts

outcomes.title: Discern and analyze context process and findings
outcomes.description:
- Paraphrase key messages and identify the text creator’s purpose and target audience.
- Analyze contextual elements and text features that inform meaning.
- Explain how societal forces and environment shape text creation and audience suitability.
- Use strategies to build background knowledge to interpret text and context.
- Reflect on how personal experience and prior knowledge influence your interpretation.

outcomes.title: Understand and interpret content
outcomes.description:
- Use a variety of strategies (e.g., questioning, predicting, annotating, close reading) to comprehend literature and other texts.
- Paraphrase a text’s controlling idea and relate supporting ideas and details; summarize and analyze plot, setting, character, atmosphere, conflict, and theme.
- Analyze characters’ traits, motivations, relationships, attitudes, and values; explain how archetypes shape meaning.
- Describe and interpret a text creator’s tone and register, and relate them to purpose, audience, and the moral or ethical stance conveyed.
- Interpret figurative language, imagery, symbols, and allusions; analyze visual and aural elements; explain how these choices—and the presenter’s performance—affect audience response and overall meaning.

outcomes.title: Engage prior knowledge
outcomes.description:
- Reflect on and describe strategies used to engage prior knowledge to comprehend new texts; select, monitor, and modify these strategies as needed.
- Assess personal expectations for texts in light of prior experiences with similar contexts, content, and text forms.
- Use metacognitive strategies to connect prior knowledge of contexts, rhetorical devices, textual elements, and structures to new understandings; identify and explain purposeful variations from conventional use.
- Classify the genre/form of new texts using attributes of previously studied genres/forms.

outcomes.title: Relate form, structure and medium to purpose, audience and content
outcomes.description:
- Identify a variety of text forms (communications and literary) and explain how form relates to purpose.
- Explain how audience factors (e.g., age, gender, culture) influence choices of form and medium.
- Identify organizational patterns and structural features, and explain how they contribute to purpose and content; assess the effectiveness of a text’s organization.
- Describe characteristics of common communication media, analyze how medium affects message, and assess whether the chosen medium suits the intended purpose, content, and audience.

outcomes.title: Relate elements, devices and techniques to created effects
outcomes.description:
- Explain how textual elements, rhetorical devices, and stylistic techniques create clarity, coherence, and emphasis, and shape atmosphere, tone, and voice.
- Recognize irony and satire in print and nonprint texts, identify the language that creates them, and analyze their effects.
- Describe and assess the effects of musical devices, figures of speech, and sensory details in print and nonprint texts.
- Explain how motif and symbol contribute to controlling idea and theme.
- Analyze elements of effective oral, visual, and multimedia presentations, differentiate effective from ineffective presentations, and identify and analyze persuasive techniques and their effects on audiences.

units.title: Personal and Narrative Writing

outcomes.title: Create oral, print, visual and multimedia texts, and enhance clarity and artistry
outcomes.description:
- Create oral, print, visual, and multimedia texts.
- Enhance clarity and artistry in these texts.

outcomes.title: Assess text creation context
outcomes.description:
- Reflect on purposes for text creation and potential consequences of your choices.
- Identify the purpose and target audience, and select strategies and text forms to engage them.
- Analyze and address audience factors that affect text creation, explaining how they shape your choices.
- Analyze expectations and constraints of the communication situation, select strategies to address them, and explain how those strategies were used.

outcomes.title: Consider and address form, structure and medium
outcomes.description:
- Select a text form appropriate to the purpose and consistent with the content.
- Use and justify structures consistent with form, content, and purpose, including complex structures as needed.
- Select an effective medium appropriate to content and context, and explain the interplay among medium, content, audience, and purpose.
- Apply the conventions of oral, print, visual, and multimedia text forms when appropriate.
- Depart from conventions when purposeful, and assess the impact on the text.

outcomes.title: Develop content
outcomes.description:
- Take ownership of text creation by selecting or crafting a personally meaningful topic, concept, or idea.
- Recognize and assess personal (experience, prior knowledge) and contextual (time, resources) variables that influence topic selection, and address them to support success.
- Establish focus and scope by framing a clear controlling idea or unifying effect.
- Develop supporting details and content suited to purpose, audience, form, and context, using appropriate developmental aids and structures.
- Incorporate effective examples from personal experience, exploration, inquiry, and research, as appropriate.

outcomes.title: Use production, publication and presentation strategies and technologies
outcomes.description:
- Meet production, publication, and display requirements for print texts, and explain choices in terms of purpose, audience, and situation.
- Develop and adapt presentation materials, strategies, and technologies to suit the purpose, audience, and situation.
- Develop and deliver oral, visual, and multimedia presentations using appropriate voice, nonverbal, and visual production factors.
- Create rapport with audiences by selecting effective strategies from a developed repertoire.

topics: Plot structure (exposition, rising action, climax, resolution)

The Writing Process Introduction - Purdue OWL®

outcomes.title: Connect self, text, culture and milieu
outcomes.description:
- Identify and reflect on personal, moral, ethical, and cultural perspectives when studying texts; monitor how your views change through interpretation and discussion.
- Respond personally and analytically to ideas in literature and other texts; analyze how ideas reflect personal and cultural opinions, values, beliefs, and perspectives.
- Form and justify positions on issues arising from text study; assess the ideas, information, arguments, emotions, experiences, values, and beliefs expressed in texts in light of personally meaningful and culturally significant issues.
- Compare and assess the choices and motives of characters and people in texts with those of yourself and others to gain insight into self and others.
- Identify, examine, and respond critically to cultural and societal influences in Canadian and international texts.

outcomes.title: Evaluate the verisimilitude, appropriateness and significance of print and nonprint
outcomes.description:
- Develop, apply, monitor, and refine criteria to evaluate the verisimilitude, appropriateness, and significance of print and nonprint texts.
- Assess your own and others’ interpretations using supporting or contradictory textual evidence.
- Analyze settings, plots, and characterization for created reality, plausibility, consistency, motivation, and contribution to theme.
- Analyze images in print and nonprint texts for created reality and appropriateness to purpose and audience.
- Assess the significance of a text’s theme or controlling idea and the adequacy, relevance, and effectiveness of its supporting details.

outcomes.title: Enhance thought and understanding and support and detail
outcomes.description:
- Assess and refine the controlling idea or unifying effect of a text in progress to meet the intended purpose.
- Review supporting details (events, images, facts, data) for accuracy, specificity, precision, vividness, and relevance; add, modify, or delete as needed for complete and effective development.
- Evaluate reasoning for logic and the consistency, completeness, and relevance of evidence; detect and correct fallacies and strengthen arguments.
- Review critical/analytical responses to literature for plausible, appropriate interpretations and precise, complete, relevant evidence; revise as necessary.

outcomes.title: Enhance organization
outcomes.description:
- Assess and revise the beginning of a text in progress to establish purpose and engage the audience.
- Review and revise organizational components (e.g., paragraphs, scenes, steps) to strengthen effectiveness and contribute to intended effects (e.g., emphasis, transitions).
- Assess and revise the closing to align with purpose, show developed understanding, and achieve an appropriate effect on the audience.
- Apply unity and coherence by assessing relationships among the controlling idea, supporting ideas, and details in oral, print, visual, and multimedia texts.
- Assess and revise transitions and transitional devices to strengthen coherence.

outcomes.title: Consider and address matters of choice
outcomes.description:
- Reflect on and expand your vocabulary and repertoire of stylistic choices.
- Assess and revise diction to achieve intended effects.
- Assess and revise syntax and sentence patterns for appropriateness, clarity, and effect.
- Explain and apply stylistic techniques and rhetorical devices to create intended effects in print and nonprint texts.
- Recognize and develop personal voice through deliberate stylistic choices and practice.

units.title: Grammar, Mechanics, and Conventions

outcomes.title: Edit text for matters of correctness
outcomes.description:
- Use handbooks and electronic tools (e.g., dictionaries, thesauri, spell checkers) to support text creation.
- Apply capitalization, punctuation (e.g., end punctuation, commas, semicolons, colons, apostrophes, quotation marks, hyphens, dashes, ellipses, parentheses), spelling, underlining, and italics correctly and consistently.
- Identify and use parts of speech and sentence parts (subject, verb, predicate complement, direct and indirect object) correctly; ensure grammatical agreement, correct pronoun reference and case, appropriate modifier use, and consistent verb tense.
- Construct and revise sentences for correctness and effect: use common structures (simple, compound, complex, compound-complex); use clauses and phrases (participial, gerund, infinitive) accurately; apply appositives and parallel structure; detect and correct comma splices, run-ons, and fragments; when appropriate, use unconventional punctuation, spelling, and sentence structure for effect.
- Monitor language use: pay particular attention when using unfamiliar vocabulary, complex syntax, or sophisticated rhetorical devices; assess strengths, identify areas for growth, and set goals.

topics: Parts of speech and sentence structure

outcomes.title: Manage ideas and information
outcomes.description: - Manage ideas and information

outcomes.title: Focus on purpose and presentation form
outcomes.description:
- Select, monitor, and modify strategies to determine the depth and breadth of inquiry or research and to identify the purpose, audience, and form of presentation.
- Describe the purpose and scope of the inquiry or research; identify the target audience and potential presentation form, when applicable.
- Refine the purpose of inquiry or research by limiting or expanding the topic as appropriate.

outcomes.title: Plan inquiry or research, and identify information needs and sources
outcomes.description:
- Plan an inquiry or research project that fits the topic, purpose, audience, context, and presentation form.
- Reflect on, select, monitor, and adjust planning strategies as needed.
- Assess prior knowledge and formulate or refine questions to clarify and categorize information needs.
- Identify and predict the usefulness of information sources to address knowledge gaps.
- Choose and use appropriate strategies and technologies to gather, generate, and accurately record information.

outcomes.title: Select, record and organize information
outcomes.description:
- Reflect on, select, monitor, and adjust strategies to select, record, and organize information
- Select information and materials appropriate to purpose from a variety of print and nonprint sources
- Record information accurately and completely, and document and reference sources to avoid plagiarism
- Organize information logically (e.g., by question, category, chronology, or cause and effect)
- Follow Internet-use guidelines for privacy, appropriate sites, copyright, and proper citation

outcomes.title: Evaluate sources, and assess information
outcomes.description:
- Reflect on, select, monitor, and adjust strategies to evaluate sources for credibility, bias, and quality
- Assess sources for appropriateness to purpose, audience, and presentation form
- Evaluate the accuracy, completeness, currency, relevance, and suitability of information for the task
- Identify biases and vested interests, and explain how assumptions and spin affect credibility

outcomes.title: Form generalizations and conclusions
outcomes.description:
- Form generalizations and synthesize new ideas by integrating new information with prior knowledge.
- Draw conclusions that are appropriate to findings, reflect own understandings, and are consistent with the identified topic, purpose, and situation.
- Distinguish between generalizations and supporting evidence, and provide sufficient, relevant, and consistent support for generalizations and conclusions.
